headline: vLLM Fixes Misleading Prefix Cache Hit Rate Log
summary: vLLM PR #54990 fixes a logging bug where prefix cache hit rate showed 0.0% before any query, confusing it with all misses. Now it omits the metric when no queries have been observed, aligning with sibling cache metrics. Prometheus counters remain unaffected.
why_it_matters: Accurate logging prevents misinterpretation of cache performance, aiding debugging and capacity planning for inference engineers.

headline: TensorRT-LLM Unifies KV Transfer with Shared Backend Contract
summary: This PR introduces a shared backend contract for native KV transfer in TensorRT-LLM, defining CacheExtent, Fetches, Publishes, and Attempt. It decouples the interface from session internals, enabling Mooncake and KVCR to use the same protocol without behavior changes.
why_it_matters: This architectural refactor lays groundwork for more flexible and efficient disaggregated KV cache management, potentially enabling future optimizations in memory and latency.

headline: GKE Pod Snapshots: Slash vLLM Cold Starts
summary: New guide shows checkpointing a single-GPU vLLM server on GKE Sandbox using Pod Snapshots. Restore from snapshot instead of re-downloading weights, cutting cold start from minutes to seconds. Example uses Qwen3-32B on H100.
why_it_matters: Eliminates repeated weight loading and engine init overhead, drastically reducing time-to-first-token for large model inference on Kubernetes.

headline: KEDA + EPP becomes the recommended autoscaling path for LLM deployments
summary: The llm-d docs now lead with KEDA + EPP for autoscaling, deprecating WVA. The guide covers four signals (queue depth, pool saturation, token backlog, estimated latency) and clarifies that pending pods and contended accelerator budgets are handled via PromQL and Kueue, not WVA.
why_it_matters: Clarifies the correct autoscaling architecture to avoid race conditions and hardware misallocation, directly impacting inference latency and throughput.

headline: llm-d Docs Clarify RDMA and Multi-Node Networking for Wide-EP-LWS
summary: A docs-only PR for llm-d links networking prerequisites for wide-ep-lws, covering All-to-All RDMA (InfiniBand/RoCE) on NVIDIA DeepEP and full-mesh pod connectivity on Intel XPU. Adds provider-neutral references to RDMA and multi-node setup guides.
why_it_matters: Clear networking prerequisites reduce deployment friction for distributed inference, ensuring low-latency all-to-all communication critical for expert parallelism.

headline: llm-d Router Docs Updated for New Plugin Architecture
summary: llm-d PR #2499 migrates guides and architecture docs to reflect removed router plugins, replacing them with prefill-filter, decode-filter, encode-filter, and prefix-cache-scorer. It removes stale parser and saturationDetector guidance, documents the exact flow, and adds an example.
why_it_matters: Clarifies the updated router plugin flow, helping inference engineers correctly configure prefill/decode/encode filters and prefix caching for optimized request handling.

headline: ComPO: Zeroth-Order Preference Alignment for LLMs
summary: ComPO is a zeroth-order alignment method using comparison oracles to extract directional preference information without differentiable loss. It mitigates likelihood displacement, with convergence guarantees and improved win rates over direct methods on Mistral, Llama, Gemma, and Qwen models.
why_it_matters: Offers a memory-efficient alternative to direct preference optimization, potentially reducing training overhead for inference engineers fine-tuning LLMs.

headline: Ermes: Stateful FaaS for Edge-to-Cloud Continuum
summary: Ermes integrates state management into FaaS, jointly scheduling functions and data across edge-to-cloud nodes. It uses collections with per-collection consistency levels (sequential to eventual) and fine-grained replication, reducing latency by converting remote state accesses to local ones. Experiments show low latency under workload growth and client mobility.
why_it_matters: For inference engineers, this addresses stateful inference latency by co-locating compute and state, reducing remote data fetch overhead in distributed edge deployments.

headline: Replication-Aware Placement for Edge-Cloud FaaS
summary: This paper introduces a Binary Linear Programming model to jointly schedule functions and place data in edge-cloud FaaS, minimizing client latency under heterogeneous consistency. A topology-aware greedy heuristic approximates optimal placement with near-optimal quality at a fraction of the cost, enabling periodic reconfigurations.
why_it_matters: For inference engineers, this offers a principled approach to reduce latency by optimizing function and data placement across edge and cloud, directly impacting user-facing AI services.

headline: Fisher-Rao Metric Reveals True Human Data Ratio to Prevent Model Collapse
summary: New paper uses Fisher-Rao geometry to derive tighter bounds on the minimum human-to-synthetic data ratio needed to prevent model collapse in LLMs, avoiding vacuous high-dimensional Euclidean limits.
why_it_matters: Provides inference engineers with a theoretically grounded data-mixing ratio to maintain model stability when training on synthetic data, reducing risk of degraded outputs.

headline: HOPE: Smarter Expert Pruning for MoE Models
summary: HOPE introduces a second-order pruning objective for mixture-of-experts models, capturing cooperative expert interactions that first-order methods ignore. It outperforms baselines like REAP, especially at high pruning rates and on complex agentic tasks, enabling aggressive compression with minimal performance loss.
why_it_matters: This reduces the memory footprint of large MoE models, making them more feasible for inference deployment without sacrificing quality on complex workloads.

headline: Stop Guessing Tool Durations: Let Tools Report Progress to Cut TTFT by 20%
summary: Agent tool calls hold KV cache memory while running, and serving systems guess durations. This paper proposes tools explicitly report progress, improving cache eviction decisions. It cuts p90 TTFT after tool calls by ~20.7% vs LRU, near oracle, with no benchmark cost.
why_it_matters: Reduces post-tool-call latency and improves GPU memory efficiency by making cache eviction decisions data-driven instead of heuristic.

headline: Inference Is the Last LLM Moat
summary: As LLM models become commoditized, inference efficiency emerges as the key differentiator. Optimizing latency, throughput, and cost through techniques like quantization, batching, and kernel fusion becomes the ultimate moat for AI companies.
why_it_matters: For inference engineers, this highlights that their work on reducing latency and cost is strategically critical, not just a technical optimization.
